Standard Test Method for 
 Ammonia Nitrogen 
 in Water

This document outlines the 
testing procedures P1, which must be performed three times a week as indicated 
by 3W1 in the above title block.

This method is 
suitable for rapid routine determination of ammonia nitrogen, in steam condensates and 
demineralizer effluents.

This document initiated by chem. Sherien Abdel Samei Eldakrory, tested by chem. Hoda Hasanen, revised by 
EDEPCo. quality control chem. Wael Ahmed Tantawy, and approved by eng: Awad 
Mohamed Fathy Head Sector of Talkha PS.

This document reviewed by 
chem. Ali Ahamed Maan, tested by chem. Mahmoud Yousef Ahmed, and approved by 
chem.
Mohamed Abdel Hafez Head Sector of Central Chemical Laboratories.

Nitrogen is a 
 nutrient in the environment and is necessary to sustain growth of most 
 organisms. It exists in several forms such as nitrate, nitrite, organic and 
 ammonia.

Ammonia is a 
 colorless, gaseous compound with a sharp distinctive odor. It is highly 
 soluble in water. The extent of association or ionization in water is 
 dependent on the temperature and PH. It may also be toxic to aquatic life.

A sample aliquot 
 is Nesslerized directly and the ammonia content determined colorimetrically. Turbid 
 sample may be clarified with ZnSO4 and NaOH solution. The 
 precipitated Zn(OH)2 is filtered off, discarding the first 25 ml of 
 filtrate and ammonia is determined on an aliquot of the remaining clear 
 filtrate by direct Nesslerization.

Collect the sample in accordance with Methods D 
1066, Specification D 1192, and Practices D 3370 in ASTM. Preserve samples by the addition of 1 ml of 
concentrated sulfuric acid per litre and store at 4C. The pH should be 2 or less. Analyze 
samples within 24 h of sampling.

Glycine, 
 Hydrazine and some amines will react with Nesslers reagent to give yellow 
 color in time required for the test.

Some organic compound such as Ketones, aldehydes, alcohols, and some 
 amines may cause an off color on Nesslerization in the distillation method.

Residual chlorine must be removed 
 prior to the ammonia determination by pretreatment of the sample.

Photometer- spectrophotometer 
 suitable for absorbance measurements at 425 nm.

Nessler 
 Reagent- dissolve 100 gm of anhydrous mercuric iodide HgI2 and 
 70 gm of anhydrous-potassium iodide in a small volume of water, add slowly with 
 stirring to a cooled solution of 160 gm of sodium hydroxide in 500 ml of water, 
 dilute to1liter store in the dark for 5 days and filter twice then keep out of 
 sun light.

Sodium 
 Potassium Tartrate Solution (300 gm/L)- Dissolve 300 g of sodium potassium 
 tartrate solution in 1 Liter of water. Boil until ammonia-free 
 and dilute to 1liter.

Ammonia Nitrogen, Standard 
 Solution (1ml = 0.01 mg N)- Dry reagent grade ammonium sulfate{( NH4)2 
 SO4}for 1 h at 100C. Accurately weigh 4.718 g and dissolve in 
 water. Dilute to 1 Litre in a volumetric flask. Pipet 10 ml of this 
 stock solution to a 1 Litre volumetric flask.

Zinc Sulfate 
 Solution, (100 gm/L)- 
 Dissolve 100 gm of zinc sulfate heptahydrate (ZnSO4.7H2O) 
 in water and dilute to 1 Litre.

All reagents shall conform to the specifications of the 
 committee on Analytical Reagents of the American Chemical Society, where such 
 specifications are available.

Other grades may be used, provided that the 
 reagent is of high purity to permit its use without lessening the accuracy of 
 the determination. In addition, this water shall be free of ammonia nitrogen, 
 such water is best prepared by the passage of distilled water through an 
 ion-exchange column containing a strongly acidic cation exchange resin mixed 
 with a strongly basic ion-exchange resin.

These resins should also be selected so that organic 
 compounds which might interfere with the ammonia determination will be 
 removed.

Dilute a portion of the filtrate

 nitrogen to 50 ml in a Nesslar tube.

Add 
 2 drops of sodium potassium tartrate solution to prevent cloudy tubes, and 
 mix.

Add 1 ml of 
 Nessler solution, then wait 20-30 min and measure photometrically at 425 nm.

Technical Procedure
Title:

 Ammonia Nitrogen 
 in Water
Method B, (Direct 
 Nesslerization)
Procedure:
Using ASTM D 1426-79 
 (P1-3W1)
Introduction

testing procedures P1, which must be performed three times a week as indicated

suitable for rapid routine determination of ammonia nitrogen, in steam condensates and

Tools and Equipments
Apparatus
Photometer- spectrophotometer 
 suitable for absorbance measurements at 425 nm.
Reagents
Nessler 
 Reagent- dissolve 100 gm of anhydrous mercuric iodide HgI2 and

Work to be 
Carried Out
Add 
 1 ml of (ZnSO4 7H2O), 
 to 100 ml aliquot and mix, if 
 the sample contains turbidity.
Add NaOH solution gently until pH is about 10.5,

Calculation
Calculate the 
 ammonia concentration, in mg/L of nitrogen in original sample, as follows:
Ammonia 
 nitrogen, mg/L = {(A1000) / S}
Where:
A = milligrams of ammonia nitrogen observed, and
S = millilitres of sample.
Calculate the 
 ammonia concentration, in mg/L of ammonia in original sample, as follows:
Ammonia, 
 (mg/L) = E 1.22
Where:
E = ammonia nitrogen , mg/liter.

The precision of the method at

 0.04.
